items.title: 15 of the Highest-Yielding Dividend Stocks in the S&P 500
items.summary: VICI Properties, UPS and General Mills lead the list of the highest-yielding dividend stocks in the S&P 500. Some of the other names might surprise you.

items.title: Hormel’s 60-Year Dividend Streak Is on the Line as Its Next Raise Approaches
items.summary: Hormel's dividend has risen for six straight decades, yet each raise keeps shrinking while cash flow once failed to cover the payout. One board vote now decides whether the record grows or starts to look fragile.

items.title: Reported SEC Probe: Could Nvidia Stock Fall To $92?
items.summary: Update, Nov 23: Nvidia stock rose more than 30%, to about $166, in Monday morning trading after its board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO; his resignation had been announced Nov. 12. The board's announcement does not mention the reported SEC review of Nvidia's accounting. The $92 estimate is measured from the close before that report, so it does not change, and the other figures below are at Friday's close.

items.title: How Jell-O’s new creative platform looks to shift consumer perceptions
items.summary: The campaign, the first by Johannes Leonardo for the Kraft Heinz brand, represents its largest marketing investment in more than a decade.

items.title: General Mills vs. Kraft Heinz: Which Food Dividend Is Better for Retirees?
items.summary: Both packaged food giants yield over 6%, but one has paid dividends for 127 years and the other slashed its payout in 2019. For retirees counting on steady income, the better track record may not be the safer bet.

items.title: These Dividend Yield Traps Are Hiding in 3 Sectors Retirees Trust
items.summary: A healthcare landlord, a twice-cut utility, and two pantry giants all pay yields that look dependable to income seekers. Behind each check sits a coverage gap, a cash shortfall, or a debt load that retirees rarely stop to examine.

items.title: A 65-Year-Old With $500,000 in Kraft Heinz, Plains All American and Healthpeak Collects $2,737 a Month in Dividends. How Safe Is Each Check?
items.summary: Key TakeawaysA $500,000 portfolio split evenly across Kraft Heinz, Plains All American Pipeline and Healthpeak Properties pays about $32,800 a year in dividends, a 6. 6% yield.

items.title: Kraft Heinz vs. Coca-Cola: Here's the Stock to Buy
items.summary: Kraft Heinz's net loss and Coca-Cola's net margin tell very different stories, and the valuation gap may surprise you.
